8bitdo-pro-3-bluetooth-gamepad: Precise D-pad, TMR sticks and remappable buttons; minor gripes include loud, clicky buttons.
8bitdo-ultimate-2-wireless-controller: Low latency and a good d-pad that works well as a Steam Input and gyro pad; some get hand cramping.
8bitdo-ultimate-3e-controller-for-xbox: Standout D-pad and clean back buttons, preferred by many to the Elite Series 2; some hit firmware bugs.
asus-rog-kithara: Open-back planar sound and wide soundstage for shooters, but wired, leaky and short on mic quality.
audeze-maxwell: Outstanding sound for a wireless gaming headset, but some had drivers or ear cups fail within months.
flydigi-vader-5-pro: Adjustable sticks and extra buttons suit larger hands better than the G7 Pro; quality control is uneven.
flydigi-vader-5s-wired-controller-for-xb: Adjustable stick tension and light stick clicks, though the app and wired-only use draw complaints.
gamesir-cyclone-2: Comfortable Xbox-like shape and clicky buttons, but the D-pad and some faulty triggers disappoint.
gamesir-g7-pro: Responsive TMR sticks at a modest price, though the small shape cramps larger hands.
gamesir-g7-pro-8k-pc: Mechanical buttons and TMR sticks suit PC; a small shape cramps some hands and the D-pad is poor.
gamesir-nova-lite-2: Hall effect sticks and a handy dongle that several used for a year or more; some Bluetooth latency.
gamesir-tegenaria-lite: Cheap, light wired controller with fast polling; one finds the d-pad a bit stiff for fighting games.
hyperx-cloud-iii-s-wireless: Comfortable, good value and long battery life, though some found the sound too bass-heavy or hollow.
logitech-g-astro-a50-x: Easy switching between consoles and PC with a good mic; a few find the sound flat for positioning.
razer-blackshark-v3-pro: Positional audio for shooters and simultaneous Bluetooth, but some feel it is overpriced.
steelseries-arctis-nova-7-wireless-gen-2: Comfortable, with simultaneous Bluetooth; several returned it over the sound or lack of noise cancelling.
steelseries-arctis-nova-elite: A feature-packed all-rounder with a good mic; price is the clear sticking point.
steelseries-arctis-nova-pro-omni: Hot-swap batteries and noise cancelling, though some feel the plastic build falls short on price.
steelseries-arctis-nova-pro-wireless: Hot-swap batteries and a dock that many keep using for years; some found it heavy or clamping.
turtle-beach-stealth-pro-ii: Positional audio and swappable batteries, but the software is buggy and failed to connect for some.
razer-deathadder-v4-pro: Ergonomic shape suits larger hands, but loud, pingy clicks led several to return it.
logitech-g309-lightspeed: Medium shape with AA-battery convenience, though some find it back-heavy and a few call it pricey.
razer-viper-v4-pro: Very light and balanced, and many prefer it to the Superstrike; the main gripe is very loud clicks.
razer-deathadder-v3: Light wired ergonomic mouse seen as good value, but a few report repeated connection drops.
vaxee-xe-wireless: Very light clicks and consistent aim, but many find battery life well short of advertised.
sony-inzone-h9-ii: Light, with dongle and Bluetooth at once, though some find the sound muddy next to rivals.
zowie-fk2-dw: A wireless version of a liked low-hump shape, but several report creaking or popping clicks.
hyperx-cloud-ii: Many report around a decade of use, though the cable is the usual weak point.
lamzu-maya-x: Light, grippy shape with light clicks, but quality control varies and several find battery short.
logitech-g305-lightspeed: Shape, clicks and low price keep many coming back, but double-clicking can develop with age.
razer-viper-v3-pro: Well built and accurate, especially for claw grip; the main gripe is scroll wheel and click faults.
logitech-g-pro-x3-superstrike: Fixes the X2's weight balance and keeps fast haptic clicks; price and stock skates draw complaints.
razer-deathadder-v3-hyperspeed: Comfortable shape at a fair price, but quality control varies, with rattling or wobbly main clicks.
logitech-g-pro-x-superlight-2c: Compact shape for fingertip and claw grips, but some find it too small or slippery.
steelseries-aerox-3-wireless: Light with crisp, firm clicks; some report connection problems and a few got faulty units.
valve-steam-controller: Good sticks, paddles and trackpads, especially for large hands, but some find the buttons mushy.
razer-wolverine-v3-pro: Clicky paddles and full remapping, ranked above Elite-style rivals by several; a couple saw it fail.
finalmouse-ultralightx: Very light with a responsive sensor, but build is the main concern, with flex and creaking on some.
zowie-s2-dw: Wide shape with a gentle hump for relaxed claw grips, but the clicks are heavy and strange to some.
zowie-u2-dw: Locked-in curved shape and great side buttons; a couple found it uncomfortable, a few saw creaking.
zowie-ec1-dw: Light and solid for big hands, especially palm grip, though battery life disappoints several.
lamzu-thorn: Light ergonomic mouse several kept as their main for years, but battery life is the top complaint.
logitech-g-pro-x-superlight-2-dex: Several call its shape the best they have tried; the main gripe is wobbly or rattling buttons.
gamesir-g7-se: Hall sticks and swappable parts in an Xbox-style pad, but bumpers or triggers broke for some.
zowie-ec2-dw: Comfortable shape and strong build that many say steadies their aim, but clicks are stiff and heavy.
endgame-gear-op1-8k-v2: Wired and light with fast clicks, though the small, narrow shape does not suit palm grip.
logitech-g-pro-x2-superstrike: Haptic clicks feel fast and easy to spam, but many find it front-heavy and pricey.
